The edit is in place. Note: SwiftUI view builders (`HStack { ... }`) allow `let` statements before the final view expression only when there's a single trailing view produced — since this closure now contains `let` bindings followed by one `ShareLink` view plus a `Button` view (two views), that's fine because `HStack`'s builder combines multiple child views via `TupleView`; `let` declarations don't count as builder expressions and are allowed interspersed.

The root cause was that the compiler couldn't type-check `ShareLink(item:)` in one pass because the `item:` argument was a deeply nested expression (`ExportPipeline(...).makeShareableImage(recipe: BootstrapRecipeBuilder.makeRecipe(...), ...)`), which is the classic "no exact matches in call to initializer" failure mode in Swift's type checker for overloaded generic initializers like `ShareLink`. I fixed it in `UI/Screens/TodayScreen.swift` by extracting `dateKey`, `recipe`, and `shareableImage` into explicitly-typed local `let` bindings, then passing the simple `shareableImage` variable to `ShareLink(item:)`. No behavior changed — same recipe/image is still built and shared.
